Explain the difference between a mutex and a spinlock in two sentences.

A **mutex** puts a waiting thread to sleep via the OS scheduler when the lock is busy—polite, saves CPU, costs a context switch. A **spinlock** burns CPU cycles in a tight loop hammering the lock until it opens—great when the wait is nanoseconds, terrible when the lock holder went out for coffee.

Is P = NP? Give me the real status.

Short answer: **Nobody has proven it either way**, and a $1,000,000 Clay Millennium Prize is still sitting unclaimed. Practically every cryptographer and complexity theorist bets **P ≠ NP**, because if P = NP, verifying a proof and inventing it from scratch would take the same polynomial effort—and your bank's public-key encryption would evaporate overnight.

Why do floating-point numbers think 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.30000000000000004?

Because IEEE 754 binary64 stores numbers in base-2 fractions, and `1/10` in binary is an infinitely repeating fraction (`0.0001100110011...₂`)—just like `1/3` is `0.3333...` in base-10. Round two slightly truncated binary fractions to 53 bits of mantissa, add them together, and the rounding crumbs show up at the 17th decimal place; use `decimal.Decimal` or integer cents if you're touching money.

What happens if I run `rm -rf /` on a modern Linux box?

On modern GNU coreutils, `rm` stops you at the door with `--preserve-root` unless you explicitly pass `--no-preserve-root` like someone determined to saw off the branch they're sitting on. Pass that flag as `root`, and it unlinks every mounted filesystem—including `/proc`, `/sys`, and `/boot`—until `libc` itself vanishes and the kernel panics in an empty void.

Why is Apple Silicon unified memory so good for local LLMs compared to consumer GPUs?

Consumer PCIe GPUs trap you in a 16–24 GB VRAM box and choke on the PCIe bus the moment a model spills into system RAM. Apple Silicon bolts the CPU and GPU cores directly onto the same high-bandwidth LPDDR5X pool (up to 400–800 GB/s), so a 48 GB Mac can hold a 35B-parameter quantized model entirely in GPU-addressable memory without a single PCIe copy.

Explain SQLite WAL mode and why we use it.

In classic rollback-journal mode, writers lock out readers because SQLite modifies the main database pages in place. **WAL (Write-Ahead Logging)** appends new changes sequentially to a `-wal` file while readers keep reading a consistent snapshot from the main file—giving you concurrent reads during writes and much faster commits (`fsync` on sequential appends).

What is the Kelly Criterion and why do traders blow up using full Kelly?

The Kelly Criterion (`f* = (bp - q) / b`) maximizes the expected logarithm of wealth over infinite trials—assuming you know your exact win probability `p` and payoff odds `b` to the last decimal place. Traders blow up on full Kelly because real-world edge estimates have fat-tailed error bars, and overbetting Kelly by even 2x drives long-run growth negative while subjecting you to stomach-churning 50%+ drawdowns; pros use **half-Kelly** or **quarter-Kelly**.

How do parameterized SQL queries prevent SQL injection in Python sqlite3? Give a one-line code example.

Parameterized queries send the SQL structure and the user input separately so the database engine treats `?` placeholders strictly as literal values rather than executable SQL syntax:

Explain why O(1) hash table lookups can degrade to O(n) and how modern languages stop hash-flooding DoS attacks.

When every key hashes to the same bucket—either by bad luck or because an attacker crafted thousands of colliding strings—your hash table turns into a glorified linked list with **O(n)** lookup time. Modern runtimes like Python (`SipHash-1-3`), Rust, and Go seed their hash functions with per-process cryptographic randomness at startup so attackers can't predict collisions offline.

What is the difference between `asyncio.gather` and `asyncio.TaskGroup` in Python 3.11+?

`asyncio.TaskGroup` provides structured concurrency: if any child task raises an unhandled exception, it automatically cancels all sibling tasks in the group and raises an `ExceptionGroup`, whereas `asyncio.gather` leaves other tasks running in the background by default.

Why should passwords be hashed with scrypt or Argon2 instead of SHA-256?

SHA-256 is designed to be fast on GPUs and ASICs (billions of hashes per second), making brute-force attacks trivial, whereas `scrypt` and `Argon2` are deliberately slow and memory-hard so each guess requires significant RAM and compute.

What is the CAP theorem in one paragraph?

The CAP theorem says that when a network partition (**P**) inevitably slices your distributed database in half, you have to choose between **Consistency** (every read sees the latest write or errors out) and **Availability** (every node answers with whatever slightly stale data it has on hand). Since real networks drop packets all the time, 'CA' systems are a fairy tale—you're really choosing between **CP** and **AP**.

Give the exact formula for cosine similarity between two vectors A and B.
Cosine similarity is `(A · B) / (||A|| ||B||)`, the dot product of the two vectors divided by the product of their Euclidean norms.
